Cohorts: selection and materialization

Source: vignettes/cohorts.Rmd
cohorts.Rmd

A cohort decides which patients, admissions or ICU stays enter the study. In rendehR the decision comes first: the selection runs in DuckDB over the raw files, and only the selected rows, together with the context they need, are written to Parquet or DuckDB. Nothing is imported before the cohort is known.

ehr_init_project(
  "mimic_iv_demo", base_dir = "cohorts-demo",
  raw_data_root = normalizePath("rendehr-demo/data/source_data")
)

The examples below use the MIMIC-IV demo downloaded in vignette("rendehR"); raw_data_root points at that copy, so nothing is downloaded twice.

Where the cohort can come from

Any cohort request is one of six routes, and at most one may be given:

You have Pass
A list of identifiers direct_ids_path
SQL that returns identifiers cohort_sql (plus optional setup_sql)
An R function that returns identifiers cohort_fn
A table of ICD codes icd_filter_path
A definition bundled with the package cohort
The whole source no_filter = TRUE

With none of them, the project’s cohort.profile and cohort.icd_filter_path decide. The profile defaults to "generic"; under "scid", comorbidities and injury severity run unless switched off.

list_example_cohorts()[, c("name", "kind", "description")]
#>      name kind
#> 1    scid  icd
#> 2 sepsis3  sql
#>                                                                 description
#> 1 Spinal cord injury - bundled ICD-9/10 list (the package reference cohort)
#> 2  Sepsis-3 (Singer 2016): SOFA >= 2 + suspicion of infection, per ICU stay

scid is an ICD-code cohort; sepsis3 runs the packaged Sepsis-3 SQL. The SQL definitions and their variants are described in vignette("sepsis-cohort-definitions").

Look before you import

select_cohort_ids() runs the selection and returns a plan without writing anything. Printing the plan reports the route, the key, the scope and the counts; identifiers never appear on screen.

scid <- select_cohort_ids("mimic_iv_demo", cohort = "scid")
sepsis <- select_cohort_ids("mimic_iv_demo", cohort = "sepsis3")
no_filter <- select_cohort_ids("mimic_iv_demo", no_filter = TRUE)
scid
#> rendehR cohort selection: mimic_iv_demo
#> Route    : named_icd
#> Keys     : selection hadm_id, evidence hadm_id
#> Scope    : requested -, effective subject_id
#> Counts   : 15 requested, 15 matched, 0 unmatched
#> Identifiers are in $values (not printed).

The plan records selection_key and selection_grain (what you supplied), evidence_key and evidence_grain (what the definition matched), the requested and effective scope, and requested_count, matched_count and unmatched_count. The normalised identifiers are in plan$values, for code that needs them, not for printing.

Identifiers, SQL, and ICD lists

A direct identifier file may be CSV, CSV.GZ, Parquet or RDS. Identifiers are read as text, trimmed, deduplicated and matched against the source hierarchy. A selection fails when the file is empty, malformed or wholly unmatched; a partly unmatched selection fails too unless allow_unmatched_ids = TRUE, and even then at least one identifier must match.

ids <- file.path(docs_root, "demo-patients.csv")
write.csv(data.frame(subject_id = c(10002428, 10000032)), ids, row.names = FALSE)
by_id <- select_cohort_ids(
  "mimic_iv_demo", direct_ids_path = ids, key = "subject_id"
)
by_id
#> rendehR cohort selection: mimic_iv_demo
#> Route    : direct_ids
#> Keys     : selection subject_id, evidence subject_id
#> Scope    : requested -, effective subject_id
#> Counts   : 2 requested, 2 matched, 0 unmatched
#> Identifiers are in $values (not printed).

SQL is an ordinary query over the source’s raw tables. Use setup_sql for any temporary objects the final query needs.

by_sql <- select_cohort_ids(
  "mimic_iv_demo",
  cohort_sql = "SELECT subject_id FROM patients WHERE gender = 'F'",
  key = "subject_id"
)
by_sql
#> rendehR cohort selection: mimic_iv_demo
#> Route    : sql
#> Keys     : selection subject_id, evidence subject_id
#> Scope    : requested -, effective subject_id
#> Counts   : 43 requested, 43 matched, 0 unmatched
#> Identifiers are in $values (not printed).

An ICD list is a CSV or RDS with icd_code and icd_version (9 or 10). icd_version is required for MIMIC-IV and eICU and optional for MIMIC-III, where ICD-9 is assumed; a code matches only in the version it names. The bundled scid cohort is exactly such a list.

Scope and context

The selected identifier sits somewhere in the source hierarchy: a patient has admissions, and an admission has ICU stays. import_scope says how much of that hierarchy to keep:

Scope Keeps
patient (default) Every admission and ICU stay of a selected patient
hospital Every ICU stay of a selected admission, plus the admission
icu Only the selected ICU stay

An ICD cohort on MIMIC selects hospital admissions, so icu cannot narrow it further; eICU selects ICU stays and accepts all three scopes.

The materialized hierarchy records the decision in three logical columns: definition_filter_index marks the unit the original definition selected, scope_index marks the units kept under the effective scope, and patient_context_index marks everything belonging to the reached patients. Selecting ICU stay I1 of patient P1 with patient scope keeps all of P1’s rows, marks I1 in definition_filter_index, and marks all of them in scope_index. The same selection with ICU scope keeps the same hierarchy but marks only I1 in scope_index.

The visit windows keep the whole patient context so concepts can look back across readmissions. Their in_scope column is the effective scope, and the cohort tables carry cohort_index, the active membership flag downstream stages read. Rows with in_scope = FALSE are context only: their events were not imported.

Materializing

Two destinations implement the same selection, hierarchy and table rules. Choose Parquet when PostgreSQL is the eventual home:

import_cohort_general(
  "mimic_iv_demo",
  cohort = "scid",
  tables = c("patients", "admissions", "icustays"),
  show_progress = FALSE
)

The import writes the filtered tables and the window and hierarchy tables next to the project:

list.files("cohorts-demo/data/cohorts_data/mimic_iv_demo_parquet")
#>  [1] "admission_windows.parquet"        "admissions.parquet"              
#>  [3] "cohort_hierarchy.parquet"         "cohort_icd_evidence.parquet"     
#>  [5] "cohort_manifest.json"             "cohort_meta.parquet"             
#>  [7] "cohort_projection_report.parquet" "cohort_table_report.parquet"     
#>  [9] "d_scid_icds.parquet"              "icu_windows.parquet"             
#> [11] "icustays.parquet"                 "patients.parquet"                
#> [13] "visit_windows.parquet"

Choose a persistent DuckDB file when DuckDB is the destination:

materialize_cohort_duckdb(
  "mimic_iv_demo",
  db_path = "cohorts-demo/data/duckdb/scid.duckdb",
  cohort = "scid",
  tables = c("patients", "admissions", "icustays"),
  show_progress = FALSE
)

Both destinations build the replacement in staging, validate it, and publish it atomically. A failed build leaves the previous cohort untouched, and the package keeps no run-version history: one current cohort and one manifest.

The Parquet output contains:

<requested tables>.parquet
admission_windows.parquet
icu_windows.parquet
visit_windows.parquet
cohort_hierarchy.parquet
cohort_meta.parquet
cohort_projection_report.parquet
cohort_table_report.parquet
cohort_icd_evidence.parquet   # ICD routes only
d_<name>_icds.parquet         # ICD routes only
cohort_manifest.json

The DuckDB file contains the same tables plus the hierarchy views cohort_patient_context, cohort_definition_filter and cohort_scope.

Narrowing later

The three indexes let later code narrow the cohort without losing the original meaning:

-- every row of every reached patient
SELECT * FROM cohort_hierarchy WHERE patient_context_index;

-- the units the definition selected
SELECT * FROM cohort_hierarchy WHERE definition_filter_index;

-- the units materialized under the effective scope
SELECT * FROM cohort_hierarchy WHERE scope_index;

cohort_index on the visit windows and cohort tables is the same membership flag the pipeline stages read, so filtering on it keeps the cohort definition intact.

The Sepsis-3 helper

build_sepsis_cohort() wraps the sepsis route when you want the packaged selection as a file, an import, or both. It defaults to import_scope = "hospital" and offers four variants through bundle:

build_sepsis_cohort("mimic_iv_demo", bundle = "first_sepsis3")

sepsis3 keeps every qualifying ICU stay, first_sepsis3 restricts to the patient’s first-ever ICU stay when it qualifies, sepsis3_admission requires the qualifying suspicion within one day of ICU admission, and first_sepsis3_admission applies both restrictions. vignette("sepsis-cohort-definitions") explains the clinical definitions and their counts on each source.

What to remember

  • One route per request; the plan is read-only until you materialize.
  • import_scope controls what is kept; the definition membership is separate.
  • Parquet and DuckDB use the same selection engine and the same indexes.
  • A replacement is atomic; an interrupted import never destroys the last good cohort.
